UI-003d.note: Assets index + detail + signed preview. C1 was a real defect: both the policy and the minting service resolved StorageManager::defaultName() instead of the provider the asset records, which signs the wrong backend, breaks when two backends share a path, and silently moves every historical asset when storage.default changes. Both call sites now resolve provider($asset->disk); unknown or unreachable means preview unavailable with no fallback. C2 adds a 60/minute per-user budget for minting only. C3 makes success and refusal alike no-store.

notes.portability: $table->json() is forbidden platform-wide. MariaDB's json is an alias for longtext/utf8mb4_bin while MySQL 8's is a native binary type, so one migration yields two types with two comparison semantics. Use ->longText() with an Eloquent array cast. Enforced by PortabilityTest::no_engine_specific_construct_is_used_in_any_migration.
notes.capabilities: FFmpeg is a capability, never a dependency. SANITUBE_MEDIA_ANALYSIS_REQUIRED defaults to false so a cPanel host without ffprobe still produces promotable candidates.
notes.catalogue_writes: Promotion is the only v1 write that creates a Track. It always creates it DRAFT, mints no ISRC, and is refusable for six reasons each carrying a machine-readable code. One-master-one-track is enforced in PromoteTrackCandidate rather than by a unique index, because tracks is ARCH-002's validated schema.
notes.ci_triggers: The workflow only built pull requests whose base was main, so a PR stacked on another claude/** branch showed zero checks — indistinguishable from a repo with no CI. The pull_request branch filter now includes 'claude/**'. Fixed on the CAT-001 branch; it reaches main when that branch merges.
notes.migration_rollback: MySQL and MariaDB drop the index they generate for a foreign key once a user-created index can serve it. A migration that adds a unique index on an FK column must therefore drop the foreign key before dropping that index in down(), then restore it. SQLite enforces none of this, so a local rollback check on SQLite proves nothing about the server engines. Enforced by PortabilityTest::an_index_added_over_a_foreign_key_column_is_undone_in_the_right_order.
notes.ai_disabled_provider: The disabled AI provider is named 'none', never 'null'. Laravel's Env::get() turns the literal string null in a .env file into PHP null, so SANITUBE_AI_PROVIDER=null yields an empty provider name and the env() default never applies. Empty/absent/null configuration normalises to 'none' at AiManager::normaliseProviderName(); an unknown non-empty name is an error.
notes.no_hosts_in_php: PortabilityTest rejects any absolute http(s) host in PHP, config included. Vendor endpoints come from the environment with no PHP default; .env.example ships the public URLs.
notes.generation: Generation never creates a Track: a selected result becomes a VERIFIED asset and a TrackCandidate with source GENERATED, which CAT-001 reviews. commercial_rights_status defaults UNKNOWN and is never inferred from a successful generation. Polling is bounded twice — the job re-dispatches only while pollable, and the service fails the generation at max_polls.
notes.release_mutation: ReleaseMutationPolicy is the single place that says which edits a status permits. DRAFT allows everything; READY allows nothing structural but can be reopened to DRAFT; SUBMITTED/DELIVERED/LIVE/TAKEN_DOWN allow nothing and cannot be reopened. I4 is called, never reimplemented or relaxed.
notes.track_numbering: release_tracks carries UNIQUE(release_id, disc_number, track_number). Renumbering must be two-phase — park every row above the occupied range, then write final numbers — because a row-by-row update collides the moment a track moves into a slot another has not yet left.
notes.distribution: Submission is the one irreversible act. Three guards against a duplicate delivery: UNIQUE(release_id, provider), a guarded status UPDATE, and a derived (not random) idempotency key sha256(release uuid|distributor). Outage != rejection: unreachable and unconfigured both produce validation errors, an outage during submit leaves the delivery FAILED and retryable. DIST-001 never mints an ISRC or UPC — a missing one is a validation error.
notes.identity: Session auth on Laravel's users table. Three roles (OWNER/ADMIN/MEMBER). role and is_active are NOT mass-assignable — set them with forceFill. Wrong password, unknown email and deactivated account answer identically to prevent account enumeration. Throttling is per email AND per IP. No self-registration: accounts come from sanitube:user:create.
notes.translation_gate: tests/Feature/Localization walks EVERY file in lang/en and checks all configured locales both directions. Any new UI string needs en/fr/es/it/pt/de or CI fails.
notes.design_system: Semantic tokens only (--color-surface, never --color-zinc-900). Status colour is decided in StatusBadge alone; labels always come from translations. Navigation is built server-side and unbuilt sections show as disabled — 'available' is presentation, never authorisation. MetricCard takes number|null and renders null as an em dash, never 0.
notes.frontend_toolchain: @vitejs/plugin-vue@5 peers Vite ^5||^6; the project is on Vite 7. Resolved with plugin-vue@6 (which supports Vite 7), NOT --force or --legacy-peer-deps: a peer conflict is compatibility information, and overriding it keeps the incompatibility. Same for vue-tsc@3. npm run types runs in CI.

review_policy.rule: Implement, get CI green, open the PR, write the report — then STOP. Do not merge. The owner sends the report to architectural review and reports the verdict; only then merge.

next_action.note: Branch from main. Independent of the UI-003d review, so it can proceed in parallel. Batch + jobs + resumable state; no transaction spanning hundreds of files; a partial failure must not roll back the successes; the browser must not need to stay open; existing ISRC/UPC preserved and never regenerated; provenance LEGACY_IMPORT. asset_preview_url.status: arbitrated by review, binding for UI-003b
asset_preview_url.rule: No signed URL is ever included in the Asset detail payload at page load.
asset_preview_url.why: A signed URL is a temporary bearer credential. Minting one on every detail view needlessly widens its lifetime and its exposure surface.
asset_preview_url.flow: Asset detail -> user clicks Preview -> authorised UI action -> backend verifies permission and asset kind/status -> mints short-lived signed URL -> browser receives it
constraints: never disk, path, bucket or credentials
VERIFIED required for an audio master
minted on demand, never on the detail GET
URL never persisted in the database
full URL never written to logs
if the provider cannot issue temporary URLs: show Preview unavailable, never make the object public
